procedural_history.originating_court: Trial Court (inferred, as the High Court decision is an appeal)
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 14.08.2008 of the High Court of Madras at Madurai Bench in Criminal Appeal No. 875 of 2002
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Madras at Madurai Bench dismissed Criminal Appeal No. 875 of 2002.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant(s) appealed the High Court's decision to the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeals.

directions: The appellants are to surrender to custody within a period of eight weeks to serve the remaining sentence failing which they shall be taken to custody.
A copy of this order be sent to the concerned trial court for necessary action.

issue.issue_text: Whether the criminal appeals filed against the judgment of the High Court of Madras should be allowed.

facts: The appellants were convicted under Sections 7 and 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and sentenced to one year of rigorous imprisonment.

The appellants' counsel argued that the evidence of a key witness (PW-2) was uncorroborated, that one appellant (A-1) did not receive any money, and that there was no evidence of a demand by the other appellant (A-2).
application: The Supreme Court heard the arguments from the appellants' counsel.
The Court considered these submissions and reviewed the depositions of the witnesses, the lower court's judgment, and the other materials on record.
reasoning.conclusion: After reviewing the arguments and the case materials, the Court dismissed the appeals and ordered the appellants to surrender to custody to serve their sentences.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the criminal appeals filed against the judgment of the High Court of Madras should be allowed.
appellant_arguments: The evidence of the key witness (PW-2) remains uncorroborated.
Accused 1 (A-1) was not in receipt of the money.
There was no evidence to show that there was any demand by Accused 2 (A-2), and therefore the conviction of A-2 is not sustainable.
respondent_arguments: The evidence of the key witness (PW-2) is corroborated by the evidence of PW-6, the office assistant.
PW-6 stated that PW-2 went inside the room of A-1, and A-1 told A-2 that PW-2 would give money and that A-2 must take and keep it, which A-2 then did.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The Supreme Court will not interfere with concurrent findings of fact by lower courts that have resulted in a conviction, especially when those findings are based on evidence that has been duly corroborated.
obiter: The testimony of a complainant in a bribery case can be corroborated by the evidence of another witness who observed the accused directing the transaction and the co-accused receiving the money.
Even the testimony of a witness who has turned hostile can serve as partial corroboration to the extent that their examination-in-chief supports the primary witness's account.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court found that the testimony of the key witness (PW-2) regarding the demand and acceptance of the bribe was sufficiently corroborated by the evidence of two other witnesses (PW-3 and PW-6) and the positive result of a test conducted in a sodium carbonate solution. Given these corroborating factors, the court saw no reason to overturn the concurrent findings of guilt by the Trial Court and the High Court.
legal_tests_applied: Deference to concurrent findings of fact by lower courts, where the appellate court will not interfere unless there is a compelling reason or a 'good ground to take a different view'.
why_appellant_lost: The appellant's argument that the evidence of the key witness (PW-2) was uncorroborated was found to be incorrect.
The court determined that PW-2's evidence was corroborated by PW-3, who, in his Chief-Examination, stated that he accompanied PW-2 who met A-1 and paid money to A-2 on A-1's direction.
The court also found that PW-2's evidence was further corroborated by PW-6, the office assistant, who testified that A-1 told A-2 that PW-2 would give money and that A-2 must take and keep it.
The court found no good ground to take a different view from the concurrent findings of the Trial Court and the High Court, which had already found the appellants guilty based on the evidence.
why_respondent_won: The respondent successfully demonstrated that the evidence of the key witness (PW-2) was corroborated by other evidence on record.

The evidence of PW-6, the office assistant, directly supported the prosecution's case by stating that PW-2 went inside A-1's room and that A-1 instructed A-2 to take the money from PW-2, which A-2 then did.
The prosecution's case was also supported by the test conducted in the sodium carbonate solution.
